top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B038) is the best-bounded discovery on the slate. Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed trade analysis from industries to firms. The model added a reallocation channel for the gains from trade that is distinct from the scale-economies and location results recognised in 2008. Its selection and reallocation predictions have been tested on customs and production microdata for more than twenty years. Exporter-premia facts predated the model, so the strongest confirmation is for the mechanism, not for welfare magnitudes, and the citation should rest on the mechanism. Attribution is the main reservation, because Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have serious related claims, but a two-name set tied to the selection model is defensible. P002 (B015) ranks second. It has the larger policy footprint, but the three-name credit is contestable and the micro evidence on Calvo-type pricing is mixed. P003 (B036) has high-quality identification but a boundary problem over whether Dorn or Katz belongs. P004 (B050) is cleanly attributed but its collateral channel is less directly identified. A prize for any proposal is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: No tie to Helpman, Melitz, Redding or the other credited names on the slate is apparent from the profile. Disclosed without adjudication: I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen, and Hassler supports P002, which I rank second and treat as evidence only. I share an SSE affiliation with other members. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a public fact for which the profile shows no bearing on committee work. My industrial-organisation and international-pricing field is adjacent to P001 and may bias my weighting.
